title: test(publish-smoke): build the scaffolded project, and assert its identity first
body:
Fixes #8678

`scripts/publish-smoke.sh` went straight from `npm install` to `objectstack dev`. `npm run build` — the **second** command the scaffolder prints — was never run, so the gate was structurally unable to see the one failure class it exists to catch.

## The evidence that this was a real blind spot

Every "published scaffold is broken" incident so far surfaced at build, and at build only:

| Incident | What broke | scaffold | install | build |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #4902 | all five remote templates at once | 0 | 0 | **2** |
| #7644 | the namespace rewrite on 16.1.0 | 0 | 0 | **2** |
| #8677 | retired `enable.trash` / `enable.mru` on 17.0.0 | 0 | 0 | **2** |

Scheduled run **#1932 concluded SUCCESS on 2026-08-10** against a published `create-objectstack` whose scaffold failed its first build on four templates. That green was honest, and it meant nothing — which is the definition of a vacuous gate.

## What the new section 1b does

**1. Asserts the project's identity before building.** This is the part that makes the gate capable of failing, and it is not cosmetic. The scaffolder's namespace rewrite only does anything when the project namespace differs from the template's own — and #7644 was precisely a rewrite that silently did nothing. Measured both ways against the #7644 state (`create-objectstack@16.1.0`):

- project namespace ≠ template namespace → build reports **4** `missing the package namespace prefix` errors, exits 2
- project namespace = template namespace → the same defect yields **0** such errors, and the whole class goes invisible

`APP_NAME` differing from the template namespace was **accidental** before this PR. Now it is asserted, with a failure message that names the remedy.

**2. Runs the build**, with the package manager that owns that project's `node_modules` (`pnpm` in pack mode, `npm` in registry mode).

**3. Refuses a build that emits nothing.** Exit 0 alone is not the assertion — a build producing no `dist/objectstack.json` would satisfy it while leaving `objectstack start` with no artifact to serve. That is a false green of exactly the kind this gate is supposed to stop, so it is checked separately.

**4. Makes absence loud.** If the template stops shipping a `build` script, the run would otherwise fail with a package-manager "missing script" message that says nothing about the template. It now names the real remedy instead.

**5. Splits the failure issue by owner.** The canary's auto-filed issue previously attributed every failure to the #3091 `^`-range class. It now tells the reader to check *which* step failed, because a build failure is a `create-objectstack` bug and an auth/CRUD failure is the dependency-drift bug — different owners, different fixes.

## Cost

Measured on GA 17.0.0 (Node 22.22.2 / npm 10.9.7): scaffold 2s, install 60s, **build 3s**. The install was already being paid for, so the added cost of this coverage is **~3s** against a job budgeted 25 minutes.

## One assumption in the card that no longer holds

#8678 weighed this against the cost of "five extra installs". That concern is moot: the five remote templates were delisted and are unmaintained, and the scaffolder's catalog is `blank` alone (`packages/create-objectstack/src/template-registry.ts`). Scope here is `blank` for the same reason — it is the entire supported surface, and the whole first-run experience for a new user.

## Scope

Two files, both CI infrastructure: `.github/workflows/publish-smoke.yml` (header comment + the auto-filed issue body) and `scripts/publish-smoke.sh` (section 1b). No published package source changes, so no changeset — `skip-changeset`.
